arxiv-2105-11500.title: Measuring Higgs Boson Self-couplings with 2 → 3 2\rightarrow 3 VBS Processes
arxiv-2105-11500.creator: Junmou Chen, Chih-Ting Lu, Yongcheng Wu
arxiv-2105-11500.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Junmou Chen, Chih-Ting Lu, Yongcheng Wu. We study the measurement of Higgs boson self-couplings through 2 → 3 2\rightarrow 3 vector boson scattering (VBS) processes in the framework of Standard Model effective field theory (SMEFT) at both proton and lepton colliders.

arxiv-2212-03975.title: Symmetry-based computational search for novel binary and ternary 2D materials
arxiv-2212-03975.creator: Hai-Chen Wang, Jonathan Schmidt, Miguel A. L. Marques, Ludger Wirtz, Aldo H. Romero
arxiv-2212-03975.description: Abstract We present a symmetry-based systematic approach to explore the structural and compositional richness of two-dimensional materials. We use a “combinatorial engine” that constructs candidate compounds by occupying all possible Wyckoff positions for a certain space group with combinations of chemical elements. These combinations are restricted by imposing charge neutrality and the Pauling test for electronegativities.

arxiv-2301-10264.title: Linking Anomalous Behaviour with Stellar Properties: An Unsupervised Exploration of TESS Light Curves 2023 Linking Anomalous Behaviour with Stellar Properties: An Unsupervised Exploration of TESS Light Curves – Linking Anomalous Behaviour with Stellar Properties: An Unsupervised Exploration of TESS
arxiv-2301-10264.creator: Dennis A Crake, Juan Rafael Martínez-Galarza
arxiv-2301-10264.description: Abstract With the upcoming plethora of astronomical time-domain datasets and surveys, anomaly detection as a way to discover new types of variable stars and transients has inspired a new wave of research. Yet, the fundamental definition of what constitutes an anomaly and how this depends on the overall properties of the population of light curves studied remains a discussed issue.

arxiv-2406-05011.title: ComplexityMeasures.jl: scalable software to unify and accelerate entropy and complexity timeseries analysis
arxiv-2406-05011.creator: George Datseris
arxiv-2406-05011.description: Abstract Abstract In the nonlinear timeseries analysis literature, countless quantities have been presented as new “entropy” or “complexity” measures, often with similar roles. The ever-increasing pool of such measures makes creating a sustainable and all-encompassing software for them difficult both conceptually and pragmatically.

arxiv-2407-19451.title: Perm: A Parametric Representation for Multi-Style 3D Hair Modeling
arxiv-2407-19451.creator: Chengan He, Xin Sun, Zhixin Shu, Fujun Luan, Sören Pirk, Jorge Alejandro Amador Herrera, Dominik L. Michels, Tuanfeng Y. Wang, Meng Zhang, Holly Rushmeier, Yi Zhou
arxiv-2407-19451.description: Abstract We present Perm , a learned parametric representation of 3D human hair designed to facilitate various hair-related applications. Unlike previous work that jointly models the global hair structure and local curl patterns, we propose to disentangle them using a PCA-based strand representation in the frequency domain, thereby allowing more precise editing and output control.

arxiv-2503-05198.title: The JCMT BISTRO Survey: Unveiling the Magnetic Fields around Galactic Center Facilities: James Clerk Maxwell Telescopy (JCMT)
arxiv-2503-05198.creator: Meng-Zhe Yang, Shih-Ping Lai, Janik Karoly, Kate Pattle, Xing Lu (呂行), David Eden, Sheng-Jun Lin, Frédérick Poidevin, Ekta Sharma, Jihye Hwang, Lapo Fanciullo, Mehrnoosh Tahani, Patrick M. Koch, Shu-ichiro Inutsuka, Valentin J. M. Le Gouellec, Hao-Yuan Duan, Jia-Wei Wang, Gary Fuller, Ray S. Furuya,
arxiv-2503-05198.description: Abstract We acquired 450 μ \rm\upmu m and 850 μ \rm\upmu m dust continuum polarization observations toward the inner region of the Central Molecular Zone (CMZ) as part of the B-Fields In Star-Forming Region Observations (BISTRO) survey using the POL-2 polarimeter on the James Clerk Maxwell Telescope.

arxiv-2512-20139.title: Challenge of nuclear transmutation in heavy-ion colliders
arxiv-2512-20139.creator: I.A. Pshenichnov, S.D. Savenkov, A.O. Svetlichnyi
arxiv-2512-20139.description: Abstract We investigate the production of secondary nuclei in the hadronic fragmentation and electromagnetic dissociation (EMD) of 20 Ne beams at the LHC and 124 Xe beams at NICA. For light nuclei at LHC energies, our calculations show that hadronic interactions are the dominant channel for nuclear transmutation.

arxiv-2604-07228.title: Emergence of cooperation in nonlinear higher-order public goods games Preprint: APS/123-QED
arxiv-2604-07228.creator: Jaume Llabrés, Onkar Sadekar, Federico Malizia, Federico Battiston

pmc-10605198.title: Nutritional Status of Children with Newly Diagnosed Food Allergies
pmc-10605198.creator: Martyna Jasielska, Anna Buczyńska, Piotr Adamczyk, Urszula Grzybowska-Chlebowczyk, Nataša Marčun Varda, Gianvincenzo Zuccotti, Ann-Marie Malby Schoos
pmc-10605198.description: Background: Most published pediatric guidelines on food allergy highlight the importance of nutritional counseling and dietary adequacy to avoid either growth retardation or nutritional deficiencies. The aim of the study was an assessment of the nutritional status of children with IgE-mediated food allergies.

pmc-10710362.title: A Peculiar Cause of Shock: Analysing Two Clinical Cases
pmc-10710362.creator: João Oliveira, Alberto Costa-Silva, Luís Vale, Daniel Costa, Rui Almeida-Pinto, Carlos Martins-Silva, Tiago Antunes-Lopes, João Silva
pmc-10710362.description: Introduction Pheochromocytoma is a rare neoplasia arising from the adrenal medulla that secretes catecholamines. Those afflicted by this condition can present a wide range of symptoms. One of the most common is paroxysmic hypertension. Interestingly, although rare, some patients present with shock. We describe two cases of pheochromocytoma in which the initial presentation was shock. Case 1.

pmc-11368034.title: Umbilical cord mesenchymal stem cells in ulcerative colitis treatment: efficacy and possible mechanisms
pmc-11368034.creator: Xiaoke Jiang, Xiaoying Luo, Conghui Cai, Yangqiu Bai, Hui Ding, Han Yue, Yalong Li, Zhiyu Yang, Huimin Zhang, Yuan Liang, Cong Peng, Huanrong Huang, Min Liu, Zhenjuan Li, Yujie Shi, Shuangyin Han, Xiuling Li, Bingyong Zhang
pmc-11368034.description: BackgroundMesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) possess powerful immunomodulatory ability. This study aimed to assess the efficacy and safety of human umbilical cord-derived mesenchymal stem cells (UMSCs) in patients with ulcerative colitis (UC) and to explore the potential mechanisms.MethodsThis prospective, self-controlled clinical study was conducted at Henan Provincial People’s Hospital.

pmc-12442159.title: A rare case of purulent massive pericardial effusion in an 85- years-old male: case report
pmc-12442159.creator: Ira Vori, Setyasih Anjarwani, Cholid Tri Tjahjono
pmc-12442159.description: Introduction: Purulent pericarditis is defined as an infection in the pericardial space that produces macroscopically or microscopically purulent fluid. It was a rare but life-threatening condition. It may be primary or secondary to another infectious process. The diagnosis can only be confirmed by pericardiocentesis. Treatment must include drainage of the pericardial space combined with systemic antibiotics.

pmc-12524022.title: Understanding the Interaction Between Premature Ageing in HIV and COPD Using Epigenetic Clocks: A Case–Control Study Protocol
pmc-12524022.creator: Meritxell Gavalda, Rebecca Rowena Pena, Francisco Fanjul, Jose Luisa Valera, Borja G Cosio, Ernest Sala, Marta Gonzalez-Freire, Melchor Riera
pmc-12524022.description: Graphical abstractKeywords: HIV, COPD, Ageing, Epigenetic clocks Introduction Since the introduction of effective antiretroviral treatment, HIV infection has transformed from a fatal condition to a chronic one. However, non-AIDS-related comorbidities have become the leading cause of death among HIV patients in developed countries.

pmc-12730836.title: Lynch Syndrome in Focus: A Multidisciplinary Review of Cancer Risk, Clinical Management, and Special Populations
pmc-12730836.creator: Seyma Eroglu, Ilhan Birsenogul, Alexandra P. Bowen, Joseph F. Doyle, Stephen E. Pupkin, Joaquin Villar, Christopher M. Tarney, Edwin Gandia, Danielle M. Pastor, Juvianee I. Estrada-Veras
pmc-12730836.description: Simple SummaryLynch syndrome (LS) is the most common autosomal dominant hereditary colorectal cancer syndrome, resulting from germline pathogenic variants in the DNA mismatch repair genes MLH1, MSH2, MSH6, PMS2, and deletions in EPCAM. The spectrum of tumors associated with LS is broad, and disease phenotype is quite variable, with risk of cancer development largely dependent on the involved gene.

pmc-12749843.title: An energy aware Q-learning framework for comprehensive coverage path planning in unknown complex environments
pmc-12749843.creator: Yao Xue, Chee Keong Tan, Wai Peng Wong
pmc-12749843.description: In post-disaster search and rescue scenarios, robotic path planning must operate in unpredictable, dynamic environments where conventional coverage path planning (CPP) algorithms often struggle to adapt. To address this challenge, we propose an intelligent path planning algorithm called PERM-QN (Q-learning with priority experience replay and memory network), designed for energy-aware, complete area coverage in uncertain terrains.

pmc-12752865.title: A 36‐Year‐Old Black Male With Sickle Cell Disease and Coexisting Psychiatric Comorbidity: Utilizing Open Dialogue Practices to Overcome Stigma and Enhance Patient‐Centered Care
pmc-12752865.creator: Daniel A Schaefer, Joseph Stoklosa, Candicee Childs, Philipp Sand
pmc-12752865.description: A 36‐year‐old African American male with sickle cell disease (SCD), osteomyelitis, major depressive disorder (MDD), and alcohol use disorder presented with active suicidal ideation following a suicide attempt via increasing alcohol consumption. Diagnostic evaluation suggested MDD. Within the hospitalization, he was also diagnosed with comorbid obsessive‐compulsive disorder.

pmc-12985706.title: Involvement of the Light Signalling Components HY5 and BIC1,2 and SPA1 in Plant Responses to Elevated Daytime UV-B Doses
pmc-12985706.creator: Pavel Pashkovskiy, Anna Abramova, Mikhail Vereshchagin, Vladimir V. Kuznetsov, Vladimir D. Kreslavski
pmc-12985706.description: Plants respond to ultraviolet B radiation (280–320 nm) with an integrated reaction that includes the reception of the acting stress factor, followed by the generation of reactive oxygen species and damage to macromolecules and membrane structures, as well as changes in cellular metabolism and the formation of protective systems.

pmc-13010526.title: Role of plasma D-dimer levels as diagnostic and prognostic marker in neonatal sepsis: An insightful support
pmc-13010526.creator: Alessandro Boscarelli
pmc-13010526.description: Neonatal sepsis remains a serious health problem with significant morbidity and mortality. Clinical diagnosis at presentation is often challenging due to nonspecific signs and symptoms. Laboratory biomarkers, blood cultures, and other diagnostic/prognostic tools such as the hematological scoring system developed by Rodwell and the neonatal organ failure assessment are not considered reliable for routine clinical use.

pmc-13050856.title: MicroRNAs in thyroid eye disease: expression signatures and clinical implications
pmc-13050856.creator: Xinyu Wang, Hongyue Chen, Songwei Li
pmc-13050856.description: Thyroid eye disease (TED), also known as Graves’ ophthalmopathy (GO) or thyroid-associated ophthalmopathy (TAO), is an autoimmune orbital disease. The core pathogenic mechanism is immune dysregulation triggered by self-antigens, which activates orbital fibroblasts and leads to pathological changes such as tissue hyperplasia and fibrosis. The clinical manifestations include proptosis and eyelid retraction.

pmc-13198129.title: Dynamic J-Wave Pattern on ECG
pmc-13198129.creator: Sofia Bezati, Effie Polyzogopoulou, Aristeidis Tsakanikas, John Parissis, Vasiliki Bistola
pmc-13198129.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). An 83-year-old man was transferred to the emergency department due to an altered level of consciousness and hypothermia. In this case report, we discuss the pathophysiologic basis, evolution, and differential diagnosis of J-wave pattern on the electrocardiogram. An 83-year-old man with a history of coronary artery disease, arterial hypertension, dyslipidemia, and hypothyroidism was transferred to the emergency department after he was found on the ground with an altered level of consciousness.

pmc-13487229.title: Eco-friendly green synthesis of zinc oxide nanoparticles using Acalypha indica L. leaf extract and their incorporation into topical formulations for acne and skin infection treatment
pmc-13487229.creator: K. Kesavardhini, Hasanain A. J. Gharban, Ashish Kumar Nayak, K. Gayathri, B. Lokeshwari, A. Sabina Banu, P. Saranraj
pmc-13487229.description: Increasing incidences of acne and skin infections, antibiotic resistance, and side effects associated with synthetic dermatology have necessitated the need for safe, sustainable treatment approaches. This work describes the environmentally friendly preparation of Zinc Oxide Nanoparticles (ZnO NPs) through green chemistry by utilizing the leaf extract of Acalypha indica L.
